task: Independent owner-requested investigation of run16 DOS4GW.PIF NESTICLE hang
status: Reproduced; immediate hang mechanism confirmed. Product not modified; correct privilege/virtual interrupt repair not yet implemented or accepted.
baseline: 82241293a / P218; original published package 2aa0d5a8-ac6b-41a8-b400-986c6c9219ac; fresh identities per isolated run
observations: P144, P181 and P218 all timed out without a graphics window under identical relocated-PIF minimal-environment controls. This is not evidence of a new P218 regression.
P218 also reproduces using the original O:/winnt PIF and executable paths. No guest binaries were changed.
Hardware execution breakpoint at CCPU GP: repeated reason=30 (FAULT_CCPU_STI_ACCESS), selector error=0, CPL=3, IOPL=0, CS:IP=01c7:6b51. Byte FB is STI. GP snapshot savedIP also equals 6b51.
The exception-handler code at 6abb/6bxx matches DOS4GW.EXE (6abb pattern at file offset 888b), not DOSX.

DOSX 00c7:1774 is C4 C4 53 17, DPMI 32-bit fault-return BOP. Its return frame is 0,6b51,1c7,6,1522,19f. Hardware breakpoints at host restoration steps show DpmiFaultHandlerIret32 reaches its RET with CS:IP restored to 01c7:6b51.
STI faults again on return, reentering the same DOS4GW exception path. This is distinct from the former unbounded PATH overwrite at protected DOS4GW 6f12.
One early hardware GP sample caught DOSX 00c7:4978 STI with CPL=3 and IOPL=0, before the repeated DOS4GW-handler STI sample.
source_support: src/mvdm-host/softpc.new/base/ccpu386/c_main.c:4114 checks CPL > IOPL before STI; fault.h defines reason 30.
src/mvdm-host/dpmi32/dpmiint.c DpmiEmulateInstruction handles 0F and 8E; it has no CLI/STI compensation.
src/mvdm-host/dpmi32/modesw.c DpmiSwitchToProtectedMode sets CPL=3 without setting IOPL.

src/mvdm-guest/dpmi/486/dxutil.asm documents forcing IOPL=3 for non-WOW_x86 outer-ring transitions; WOW_x86 instead uses DPMISwitchToProtectedMode BOP. This identifies a contract to reconcile, not permission to patch the guest.
limitations: The origin/ownership of the IOPL=0 state still needs a complete transition trace. A data watch stopped after 80 early real-mode writes and did not establish that origin.

A one-time diagnostic IOPL=3 mutation did not reach graphics; it is not a proven fix. The first attempt also retained a hardware breakpoint on detach and exited 80000004 (probe artifact); the corrected cleanup attempt timed out. Neither control is product acceptance.
Read-only CPU snapshots suspend only the owned worker CPU thread; the legacy printed non-atomic label is retained. Memory dumps and compiler outputs stay in build.
No ROM gameplay, keyboard interaction or clean NESticle exit has passed. Prior visible-window-only evidence cannot establish those capabilities.
repair_direction: Reconcile the generic DPMI protected-mode privilege and virtual-interrupt contract with the CCPU backend. Preserve architectural GP checks; do not add DOS4GW-name checks, guest patches or unconditional global privilege elevation. Validate actual rendered NESticle UI/input and clean exit, not just existence of LibKvmWindow.
